issues.legal_issue: An alleged breach of a status quo order does not amount to contempt when the conduct is consistent with the state of affairs preserved by the order as properly construed.
material_facts: The Supreme Court directed the parties to maintain the status quo as in the High Court.
The High Court had decided only that slurry was not coal or a mineral and had not adjudicated the parties’ rights.
While the writ petition was pending, the High Court had permitted the respondent and his son to collect slurry subject to conditions.
After the Supreme Court’s order, the respondent and his son approached the High Court without disclosing that order and obtained an order permitting transport of briquettes.

The Supreme Court construed the status quo direction as preserving the state of affairs that existed while the writ petition was pending, including the earlier conditional permission to collect slurry.
issues.conclusion: No contempt was made out on the plain terms of the status quo order, although the respondent’s suppression of the order when approaching the High Court was deprecated.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, contempt requires conduct amounting to disobedience of the court’s order. “Status quo” ordinarily refers to the existing state of things at a given time, and qualifying words limit the order’s scope. Where the order preserves the status quo as it stood in a court while a matter was pending, and that court did not adjudicate the parties’ rights, the order preserves the state of affairs during that pending proceeding. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding alleging disobedience of a court order.
predicates.status_quo_order_limited_to_pending_proc: The order directs preservation of the state of affairs as it existed while a proceeding was pending in another court, whose decision did not determine the parties’ rights.
predicates.challenged_conduct_consistent_with_prese: The conduct alleged to breach the order is consistent with the state of affairs preserved by the order, including any permission then in force.

issues.definition: If an alleged breach is considered in a contempt proceeding, the order is limited to the state of affairs during a pending proceeding, and the challenged conduct is consistent with that state, the output is that no contempt is found.

issues.legal_issue: A State cannot rely on a later lease to authorize removal of material from land included in an acquisition declaration that also acquired the rights to work and carry away minerals.
material_facts: A declaration covered the land in dispute as part of a larger area acquired by the Central Government.
The declaration included the rights to mine, quarry, bore, dig, search for, win, work and carry away minerals in the acquired lands.
The State had granted a lease to the respondent for removal and collection of slurry from the land.
The respondent did not deny the relevant averments about the declaration and the rights it acquired.
issues.conclusion: The disputed land had been acquired together with the specified rights, and the contention that the State could grant a lease for removal and collection of slurry from it despite the declaration was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(1) of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957 provides for the acquisition declaration; Section 9(2)(b) requires the declaration to specify the acquired rights, including rights to mine and carry away minerals. The Court treated the declaration as vesting the land absolutely, free from encumbrances, with the specified mineral rights. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.land_acquisition_dispute: The dispute concerns whether material may be removed from land under a State-granted lease.
predicates.land_included_in_acquisition_declaration: The land was included in a declaration acquiring it for a public purpose.
predicates.declaration_included_rights_to_work_and_: The acquisition declaration included rights to work the land for minerals and carry them away.

issues.definition: If a land-acquisition dispute concerns land included in an acquisition declaration that also includes rights to work and carry away minerals, the output is that a later State lease cannot authorize removal.
